answer: To mitigate sybil attacks, agents must perform a recurring proof-of-stake verification where they lock tokens to gain reputation. Think of the stake as a nectar that binds the identity to the network. Every delta in the node architecture requires a new cryptographic signature, preventing cheap account cloning. If an attacker tries to register a fake marble identity, the cost of securing sufficient stake across multiple nodes becomes economically prohibitive, forcing them to burn funds rather than profit.
